Hi Priya / Monica / Alicia —

Thanks for the ping. Below are the confirmed answers and evidence pointers; I kept the language concise for the RFP. If MidState wants deeper detail we can schedule a technical call.

1) PHI inventory: attached is midstate_phi_inventory.csv with example fields we would touch in the integration (patient identifiers, encounter metadata, clinical notes). We treat images (DICOM) as file blobs that can be processed but are not parsed into structured clinical fields by default.

2) Encryption in transit: TLS 1.3 for all API traffic; mutual TLS available for Dedicated/Private deployments where required.

3) Encryption at rest: AES-256-GCM with per-tenant key wrapping. We use customer-separable key metadata and support both Redwood-managed KMS and customer-managed keys via AWS KMS/HSM for Dedicated and VPC deployments. Key rotation: default 90-day rotation for service-managed keys; customer-managed keys follow the customer's KMS policy.

4) Key ownership & HSM: For Redwood-hosted (SaaS) deployments, Redwood holds the master key unless customer requests CMK for Dedicated/Private. For HSM-backed key storage we integrate with AWS CloudHSM or equivalent — attestation documentation is in the attached encryption design.

5) Audit logging & retention: Admin and system-level audit logs are retained for 365 days by default; access logs for PHI access are stored for 1 year. Logs capture request metadata, requestor identity (token or service account), and operation type. We can export logs to a customer-owned S3/GCS bucket on request for additional retention. Per-token content traces are captured in ephemeral tracing for debugging (rotated and redacted) and are not retained to long-term storage unless explicitly enabled under a support ticket with a retention justification.

6) SOC 2 Type II: Redwood has a current SOC 2 Type II; we can share a redacted report under NDA. Redaction is performed by our security team and typically completed within 3 business days after NDA execution. See attached redwood_soc2_summary.pdf for the executive summary.

7) BAA timing: Standard BAA review & signature from Redwood side: 2-3 weeks after receipt of signed mutual NDA and initial redlines. If MidState requires an addendum (e.g., special retention or data residency clauses), plan for 4-6 weeks. If MidState prefers to use their standard BAA template, please send it early so we can triage likely redlines.

8) Evidence & attachments provided here: redwood_encryption_design.pdf (high-level templates and architecture diagrams), redwood_soc2_summary.pdf (summary), midstate_phi_inventory.csv (sample inventory).

If you want, Monica and I can join a 30-minute call next week to walk through these points with your security and legal.

Best regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Applied ML & Security Liaison | Redwood Inference
